codeReview.issue: The metadata lists hard constraints as anti-patterns: text only, no icon, and children must never be wrapped in another Text or Heading. But `children: React.ReactNode` still accepts <Icon>, <Text> or <Heading> without a type error. The 'Type-enforced anti-patterns' rule in .claude/rules/components.md says a documented hard constraint must be a TypeScript error, not only a note. The approved proposal used ReactNode without saying why it differs from this rule.
codeReview.fix: Narrow to `children: string`. This matches the brief ('Text only'), the 'pass a plain string as children' anti-pattern and the stories. Update api-proposal.md to match.

codeReview.issue: The `.filled` background (`color.background.overlay.subtle`, black-alpha-3 in light) uses the default `background-clip: border-box`, so it is painted under the translucent `color.border.strong` (black-alpha-5) border. The two alphas stack, so the drawn border is darker than the token value and different from the reference image, where the stroke is only slightly stronger than the fill.
codeReview.fix: Add `background-clip: padding-box` to `.badge` (or `.filled`) so each token renders at its own value.

codeReview.issue: `.outlined { background: transparent; }` repeats the initial value and does nothing.
codeReview.fix: Remove the `.outlined` rule. `styles[variant]` resolving to undefined is already handled by `.filter(Boolean)`. Or keep the class only as a hook, with no declarations.

a11y.issue: The filled variant draws `color.text.subtle` text on `color.background.overlay.subtle`. That pair is missing from the curated `PAIRS` list in scripts/token-contrast-check.js, which only has `T("subtle")` on `BG("overlay-subtlest")`. Nothing checks contrast for this pair in light or dark, and jsdom/axe cannot either.
a11y.fix: Add `[T("subtle"), BG("overlay-subtle")]` to PAIRS. Run `npm run tokens:contrast-check`. If it fails, record a waiver or adjust the token rather than shipping it unchecked.

a11y.issue: The metadata accessibility block (role generic, no ARIA, no keyboard contract, not focusable) matches the implementation: a plain <span> with onClick/role/tabIndex removed from the props type. But `aria-*` attributes can still be spread, so a caller can add `aria-label` to a generic span. ARIA prohibits naming the generic role, and it would hide the visible text from some assistive technology.
a11y.fix: Optionally add `'aria-label' | 'aria-labelledby'` to the Omit list so the visible text stays the only accessible content.
